falseAssumptions.correction: S2.2.8b also allows 21.3 m on sites with frontage over 60.7 m where enhanced open space is provided; the VTC block frontage (79.2 m and 144.8 m) meets the frontage test.

falseAssumptions.claim: CDDG Table 1.5 tower separation is employment-employment 15.2, employment-hotel 15.2, employment-residential 18.3 and residential-residential 24.4 m.
falseAssumptions.correction: The table also sets residential-hotel at 24.4 m (reducible to 18.3 m under S1.5.2) and hotel-hotel at 15.2 m; G1.5.1 asks for more separation where towers exceed typical heights. Use the full matrix with S1.5.2 and S1.5.3 conditions.

falseAssumptions.claim: Computed P06 checks (M03, M06, M07) evidence the 30% cultural-context jury criterion.
falseAssumptions.correction: No computed P06 check measures reconciliation or cultural context. It is a human-judgment record (M08 cultural-context log). M03 only names Indigenous-named Table 1 spaces and routes them to human review.

falseAssumptions.claim: Downtown solar rules prohibit any new shadow on all public spaces between 10:00 and 16:00 PDT.
falseAssumptions.correction: The Downtown Peninsula guidelines are tiered: no new shadow on parks, school sites and the Davie and Robson Village north sidewalks; urban plazas and miniparks to be minimised; exceptions through a rationale, 15-minute solar budget and detailed study. Time wording amended from PDT to PT on 28 July 2026.

falseAssumptions.claim: EDM Table 8-2 asks for a seat or rest spot every 50 m along busy routes (P06-M06 rest spacing).
falseAssumptions.correction: Table 8-2 gives maximum distances between resting spots by user group: wheelchair users 150 m, visually impaired 150 m, mobility impaired with a stick 50 m, without a walking aid 100 m. The busy-route 50 m rule belongs to DfT, as an external comparison.

falseAssumptions.claim: Mid-block connections of 5.4 m (non-residential), 7.3 m or 4.5 m (half share) are acceptable on the VTC block.
falseAssumptions.correction: S1.12.2c requires 9.1 m face to face for large sites or sites identified in S1.12.1, and S1.12.1b covers sites adjacent to or including a transit station entrance, which the VTC brief requires. Narrower widths only as a G1.12.1 variation.

falseAssumptions.claim: New shadow on urban plazas only needs to be 'actively minimised' (P06-M03 protected-space metric).
falseAssumptions.correction: Dilawri Square South, Jack Poole Plaza and Robson Square follow 3.1 (no new shadow, 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00, exception path 3.1.2). Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park: no new shadow 10:00-16:00 (4.1.1). Victory Square: 3.1 plus the Cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 on 11 Nov (4.3.1). Other urban plazas and West End miniparks: minimise where possible (3.2.1).

falseAssumptions.claim: Solar tests run in 'local Pacific time', with seasonal PST/PDT switching.
falseAssumptions.correction: Council report RTS 18459 states BC adopted permanent year-round daylight-saving time, and Appendix D replaces PDT with PT. The guidelines set the model to PDT (UTC-7). Use UTC-7 year-round and show the offset; Victory Square 4.3.1 still says PST (unresolved).

falseAssumptions.claim: TfL Appendix B gives 5.3 m total footway width for any flow above 1,200 pph.
falseAssumptions.correction: TfL says 5.3 m (or 3.3 m without furniture) gives comfortable movement up to 2,000 pph. Above that, derive the clear width from ppmm at B+ (pph / 60 / 11) plus buffers.

falseAssumptions.claim: TfL Figure 9 shows the high street as the most crowding-tolerant area type, and average-of-maximum guidance differs only for interchange (round-1 critic's claim; spec carried a 'confirm visually' caveat).
falseAssumptions.correction: Figure 9: high street and tourist are strictest and use the same guidance for peak and average-of-maximum; residential, office/retail and interchange relax 'at risk' in the average-of-maximum column. Spec ordering was right; caveat dropped.

falseAssumptions.claim: The 10% public open space target for mid-sized sites (S1.9.2) is a valid passing target for the VTC block.
falseAssumptions.correction: S1.9.2 does not apply: the CDDG glossary defines mid-sized sites as over 4,000 and under 8,000 m2, and the VTC block is about 11,468 m2. Default to S1.9.1 (20%), with POPS of about 10% (S1.10.2) counted inside it.

falseAssumptions.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is the policy that frames 244-305 m (800-1,000 ft) towers on the VTC site.
falseAssumptions.correction: The City's April 2026 memo says the policy was last updated in 2011 and currently allows up to 600 ft (about 183 m), with one location up to 700 ft (about 213 m). The VTC height range is above it. The review is open and draft directions are expected in late 2026.

falseAssumptions.claim: The City EDM requires street furniture at least 1.0 m from vehicle crossings and entrances.
falseAssumptions.correction: No 1.0 m figure was found in EDM 8.4.3, 8.4.9 or Chapter 9. EDM p.341 asks furniture to be set back to keep sightlines at driveways and crosswalks, typically 10 m from intersections.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Downtown (Except Downtown South) Design Guidelines and Central Area Pedestrian Weather Protection guidelines govern podium, streetwall and ground-floor design for Central Business District sites.
falseAssumptions.correction: Council approved the City-wide Design and Development Guidelines on 28 July 2026 and repealed both documents effective 27 October 2026. The CDDG now governs; its final text was not yet posted.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Granville Street Plan referred to by CDDG 4.18 was not available, so its content is unknown (P06-S40).
falseAssumptions.correction: RTS 18459 Appendix C pp.38-39 reproduces the plan's new Urban Design Framework: 24/7 destination; lighting, clear sight lines, inclusive features; queuing areas and resting spots; transit entries; screens dimmed after 22:00; towers that complement the fine grain. The DD character area descriptions remain unopened.

falseAssumptions.claim: The S2.2.7 18.3 m Downtown podium cap applies to a mixed-use tower whenever residential floors sit above, and which of S2.2.6 or S2.2.7 governs a mixed tower is unresolved (P06-M02).
falseAssumptions.correction: For the VTC tower use Table 2.2b (S2.2.6); apply S2.2.7 only to exclusively residential towers. S2.2.8b raises Table 2.2b maxima below 21.3 m to 21.3 m on frontage over 60.7 m with enhanced open space; ROW over 30.5 m already allows 23.0 m, so 21.3 m is no cap there.

falseAssumptions.claim: Transport interchanges and tourist areas tolerate less crowding than residential streets (TfL).
falseAssumptions.correction: TfL Figure 9: high street and tourist attraction are strictest (acceptable to B, at risk B-, unacceptable from C+); residential is intermediate (acceptable to B-, at risk C+); office/retail and transport interchange are most tolerant (acceptable to C+, at risk C-). B+ is recommended for all; C+ is the floor with compensation.

falseAssumptions.claim: Vancouver requires a numeric ground-floor transparency percentage.
falseAssumptions.correction: The CDDG asks for transparent glazing across most of the ground-floor facade up to the second-floor underside or canopy underside, with no percentage. Any percentage in the tool is a team assumption.

falseAssumptions.claim: Vancouver's shadow test is the 10:00-16:00 run in 15-minute steps.
falseAssumptions.correction: Every Downtown applicant submits a Basic study at two-hour intervals (5.1.1). The 15-minute Detailed study with area take-offs and the coverage formula is for applicants seeking a relaxation of 3.1.1 or 3.3.1 (5.2.1).

falseAssumptions.claim: A BC legislative session is under way in fall 2026 and may act on DRIPA (r3 critique, M02 badge note).
falseAssumptions.correction: The Assembly adjourned 28 May 2026 and the 43rd Parliament was dissolved 22 Sep 2026; a general election is on 24 Oct 2026. No sitting can act before the election. BC Laws shows the Act current to 13 Oct 2026.

falseAssumptions.claim: A downtown plaza naming precedent could not be found; the critic's Art Gallery example is unverified (r1 flag).
falseAssumptions.correction: On 18 Jun 2018 the QE Theatre plaza and the Art Gallery north plaza received names combining hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh. A committee with representatives of the three Nations chose them; the City renamed them.

falseAssumptions.claim: Contacting the one Coast Salish juror and her firm is the juror-contact risk (M01 contact_guard).
falseAssumptions.correction: Cl. 5.2 bars approaching any of seven jurors or the undefined Commissioning Party; cl. 8.3 voids prizes. The jury includes UBC SALA's Matthew Soules. The guard covers all seven jurors and firms, the Commissioning Party and Buildner's advisors.

falseAssumptions.claim: EU AI Act Article 50 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (S42 extract).
falseAssumptions.correction: A provisional Omnibus deal of 7 May 2026 reportedly moves the Art. 50(2) marking duty to 2 Dec 2026. Check formal adoption in the Official Journal. Benchmark only; not binding in BC.

falseAssumptions.claim: Every image with no AI maps to digitalCreation, with humanEdits for edited captures (M07 mapping, r3).
falseAssumptions.correction: IPTC defines digitalCreation as media created by a human with non-generative tools, so it does not fit a camera capture. Unedited photo: digitalCapture. Edited capture: humanEdits. Montage of renders and captures with no AI: composite. Montage where every element is a capture: compositeCapture.

falseAssumptions.claim: ExifTool can strip author and GPS fields from competition PDFs (M07 library role, cut #1 and the identity-field metric).
falseAssumptions.correction: ExifTool edits PDFs by reversible incremental update and never deletes old data, so original Author, Creator and XMP values stay recoverable. Pipeline now: delete /Info and XMP (pikepdf), strip image and object metadata, full qpdf rewrite, raw-byte scan, fixture test with a recovery attempt. ExifTool is for non-PDF images and read-only scans.

falseAssumptions.claim: FPIC is obtained only by States, so it is not claimable by an entrant (M02 claimable_by_entrant basis).
falseAssumptions.correction: TRC Call 92(i) asks the corporate sector to seek FPIC before economic development projects. FPIC stays locked for entrants because a hypothetical competition entry has no real project and, at N0-N3, no engagement.

falseAssumptions.claim: Local Contexts Notices are Open to Collaborate, Attribution Incomplete, TK, BC and Collections Care (S27 round 0 extract).
falseAssumptions.correction: The current page lists an Engagement Notice, Disclosure Notices (Attribution Incomplete, Traditional Knowledge, Biocultural) and Collections Care Notices, and points to Hub Agreements, an API Guide and Terms and Conditions. M05 reads Notice types from the Hub at run time and shows link-out only until the Hub terms have been read.

falseAssumptions.claim: M07 ai_involvement maps 'composite' to compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia and 'assistive edit' to algorithmicallyEnhanced.
falseAssumptions.correction: IPTC defines compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia as 'Edited using Generative AI' (inpainting, outpainting) and compositeSynthetic as a mix with at least one generative element. algorithmicallyEnhanced is non-generative only. Enum split into generative and non-generative edits; mapping rewritten.

falseAssumptions.claim: No source describes a services agreement between Sen̓áḵw and the City (r1 flag; M04 field marked unverified).
falseAssumptions.correction: The City and Squamish Nation signed a services agreement on 25 May 2022 for water, utilities, electricity, fire and police services. Tenure: reserve land; City services by agreement; no City land-use approvals needed.

falseAssumptions.claim: Per-view height rules for the 24 cones sit in the Public Views Guidelines (2024), and the 24-record dataset is a fixed match to the July 2024 set (M06).
falseAssumptions.correction: The dataset says the authoritative source for the views is the City's bylaws and that the extract is updated as needed; it was modified 19 Oct 2026. M06 links touched cones to the governing by-law or plan as well as the Guidelines, and re-checks count and ids at each export.

falseAssumptions.claim: Personal-data fields at export = 0 is a verified threshold based on S34 and S35 (M07).
falseAssumptions.correction: Status is team_assumption. The brief (S35) was not opened. The competition page confirms only anonymous evaluation, and the Terms (S47) bar marks, logos or symbols that identify the author's source. Neither text states a rule for file metadata. A human must read the brief's anonymity clause.

falseAssumptions.claim: Referral-pack completeness against the Musqueam list is a verified metric for this entry (M01).
falseAssumptions.correction: The page verifies the list of eight items, not that it applies to an ideas competition. It addresses proponents and regulators of projects with regulatory processes. Applicability to a competition entry is not established. The checklist leaves the entrant flow and survives as reference material for real projects. Default is no contact; brief questions go through the portal.

falseAssumptions.claim: S48 is an undated CIRNAC page whose title was not captured.
falseAssumptions.correction: The page is 'Updated Guidelines for Federal Officials to Fulfill the Duty to Consult', March 2011: guidance for federal officials that may be dated. It says third parties such as proponents have no legal obligation to consult.

falseAssumptions.claim: Sen̓áḵw facts in M04 (58 storeys; services list; no City approvals needed) are plain precedent facts without speaker or conflict.
falseAssumptions.correction: S54: the services list is Mayor Kennedy Stewart's statement; 'no City approvals needed' is the reporter's own. S16 gives 58 storeys and also 56 for 'some buildings'; Dezeen gives 12-58. Each fact carries a speaker tag and a conflict chip.

falseAssumptions.claim: Sen̓áḵw is an MST-led development (as framed in the packet scope).
falseAssumptions.correction: Sen̓áḵw is a Squamish Nation project led by Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, on Kitsilano Indian Reserve No. 6, with OPTrust as 50% partner in Phases 1-2. MST Development Corporation (Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh together) leads Jericho Lands and Heather Lands, with Canada Lands Company.

falseAssumptions.claim: The City view-cone dataset gives the full set of protected public views ('24 polygons of protected public views').
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat the dataset as partial until it is checked against the City's view-protection guidelines in a browser. Zero intersections is not clearance. A touched cone still needs the City's per-view height rule, which is not in the dataset.

falseAssumptions.claim: The City view-cone dataset may be partial because view numbers 1-2, 4-8, 11-19, 23-26 and letters C, F, I are absent (r1 flag and M06 metric basis).
falseAssumptions.correction: On 10 Jul 2024 Council removed 14 of 38 cones, amended 11 and left 24 under the new Public Views Guidelines. The 24 records match; no removed id (C1, C2.x, E1, E2.2, E3, F1.x, 12.1, 3.1, 3.2.4a, 9.2.2, 20.2) appears.

falseAssumptions.claim: The ICoD charter was built with input from Sami, Inuit, North American, Maori and Australian practitioners (S29 extract).
falseAssumptions.correction: The contributor appendix lists research workshops in Australia, Denmark, Greenland and Sweden (Australian Indigenous students and staff, Inuit and Sami participants). The Montreal launch panel (Oct 2017) lists Canadian and US Indigenous panelists, including a Nisga'a architect. Maori practitioners appear only as designers of featured works, not as listed contributors. No Coast Salish contributor is named. Describe the charter as Australian-led with Nordic Indigenous workshop input and a North American launch panel.

falseAssumptions.claim: The International Indigenous Design Charter's principle list could not be retrieved, so M03 links rather than paraphrases (round 0 UNVERIFIED flag and M03 limits).
falseAssumptions.correction: The full charter book is public on the ICoD site and lists ten protocols: Indigenous led; Self-determined; Community specific; Deep listening; Indigenous knowledge; Shared knowledge; Shared benefits; Impact of design; Legal and moral; Charter implementation. M03 now indexes its starter cards to these names with one-line paraphrases and a link.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Musqueam page lists eight package items and applicability to ideas competitions is ambiguous only because of item 2 (S10, M01).
falseAssumptions.correction: The page lists eight named items plus an open-ended additional-documents line, and asks for contact at initial planning of all projects within Musqueam territory. That sentence is the real source of the ambiguity. N0 stays default.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Q&A route closes 3 Nov 2026 and can settle whether a Nation-contact channel exists (M01 method, UNRESOLVED flag).
falseAssumptions.correction: Cl. 10.10: one free question per registration, due three days after registration closes (1 Nov unless the portal says otherwise), and only the five most-voted reach the jury. An answer is not assured; N0 is the standing default.

falseAssumptions.claim: The governing document is the 'Higher Buildings Policy for Rezonings (1997)' and whether it was amended is unverified (S36).
falseAssumptions.correction: City pages call it the Higher Buildings Policy: established 1997, last reviewed and updated 2011, minor upper-limit changes since, under review 2026-27. Protected views are not part of the review.

falseAssumptions.claim: The new BC government's DRIPA position is unknown (M02 badge_states, r3 flag on the legislative session).
falseAssumptions.correction: Parties' stated positions are known: S60 (critic-read r4) reports the Conservative Party said it would repeal DRIPA and a Conservative MLA applied for a repeal petition. Only the 24 Oct election result is open. Badge reads: election 24 Oct; parties' positions differ; outcome pending; re-check 25 to 27 Oct.

falseAssumptions.claim: A 15% profit on GDV is the Vancouver viability convention.
falseAssumptions.correction: The City's consultant measures profit divided by total project cost including land and treats 15% as viable, which equals 13.0% of GDV; 15% of GDV equals 17.6% on cost in the hand check.

falseAssumptions.claim: A negotiated CAC applies to the whole land lift of this mixed-use rezoning.
falseAssumptions.correction: Compute lift by use; offer toggles for CAC on residential lift versus net total lift; never allow a negative CAC; flag the exemption rule as unverified.

falseAssumptions.claim: A site over 8,000 m2 is barred from rental DCL and ACC relief.
falseAssumptions.correction: The 8,000 m2 figure is an example in the 2025-27 relief programme summary. Draft by-law s.6.1 tests tenure and rents: a wholly rental building, no strata units, CMHC-based rents and a housing agreement; a mixed rental and strata tower cannot qualify.

falseAssumptions.claim: AACE 56R-08 class ranges are hard bounds (or triangular min/max), and a design reaches Class 4 once ADVANCED presets are set.
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat the ranges as P10/P90 (80% interval after contingency); assign class by deliverable maturity; default to Class 5 for BASIC massing and supertall extrapolation.

falseAssumptions.claim: AACE Class 5 ranges (+30/+50%) apply as P10/P90 around any base the user enters, including one with no contingency.
falseAssumptions.correction: Require contingency > 0 so the base is about P50; default the supertall high side to 2x Table 1 (+60% to +100%), editable to 3x; cite the 56R-08 clause.

falseAssumptions.claim: Ahlfeldt and Barr's height elasticities (0.26 commercial, 0.56 residential) are per-floor multipliers, and the stacking order of uses changes cost.
falseAssumptions.correction: They are building-level elasticities of average cost per floor space on floor count. Apply (N/N_ref)^eps once per building with eps blended by GFA share; the stacking-order claim is removed.

falseAssumptions.claim: CBRE downtown inventory (16.57 M sf AAA+A) is comparable to the tower's net lettable area.
falseAssumptions.correction: Compare new building area (GFA) with CBRE building area; show net or rentable area only as a secondary variant.

falseAssumptions.claim: CBRE's 'no new supply for at least four years' statement is a years-to-lease benchmark.
falseAssumptions.correction: It is a supply-lag statement tied to economic rents above market rents; use it to set the earliest delivery date and the window without competing supply, not as a gauge threshold.

falseAssumptions.claim: CBRE's five-year average quarterly leasing (about 518,000 sf) can serve as the upside for downtown net absorption when computing years to lease.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use downtown net absorption (H1 2026 +103,062 sf all classes, about 206,000 sf/yr; AAA+A rows +128,448) with 0.5x/1x/2x team multipliers, and show leasing activity only as separate deal flow.

falseAssumptions.claim: City-wide DCL $49.88/m2 and Utilities DCL $39.06/m2 (consultancy blog) apply to this tower and its commercial floors.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use the City schedule: City-wide DCL $214.89/m2 for commercial & other and apartments above 1.5 FSR; Utilities DCL $67.33/m2 (commercial) or $134.65/m2 (apartments).

falseAssumptions.claim: Lee/CoStar's Metro average NNN asking rent ($46.81/sf, Q2 2026) can be used as downtown office underwriting rent.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use class-matched downtown net asking rents (CBRE AAA $48.02; all classes $34.93); an NNN figure without class and geography match fails the ledger check.

falseAssumptions.claim: Legacy CAC targets (fixed per-sf targets for rezonings) apply to a new Vancouver rezoning.
falseAssumptions.correction: For rezoning applications submitted after 30 Sep 2026, CAC targets are removed and the city-wide ACC applies (commercial $3.00/sf; apartments above 1.5 FSR $10.00/sf at 50% in year one); negotiated CACs remain for larger, complex projects.

falseAssumptions.claim: Metro Vancouver water and parkland DCCs are not yet in force (draft rates only).
falseAssumptions.correction: They are in force from 24 Jul 2026 (non-residential $5.30 and $0.24/sf; apartments $6,791 and $303/unit) and step to $7.51, $0.60, $9,630 and $763 on 1 Jan 2027.

falseAssumptions.claim: Non-residential statutory charges total about $18.1-18.4/sf (ACC + Metro DCC + TransLink DCC).
falseAssumptions.correction: Include the City-wide DCL and Utilities DCL: about $44.3-44.6/sf ($477-480/m2) for office or retail from 1 Jan 2027.

falseAssumptions.claim: Q2 2026 trade evidence is $455-542/sf, mostly Class B.
falseAssumptions.correction: Quote $359-542/sf: all three trades are Class B and two lie outside downtown; replacement cost is the primary cross-check for a new AAA tower, trades secondary.

falseAssumptions.claim: Rental developments are exempt from the ACC and from DCLs.
falseAssumptions.correction: Relief is conditional: the ACC proposal gives a 100% waiver (Class A, 20% below-market area) or 86% (Class B, CMHC average rents); all rentals still pay the Utilities DCL; DCL relief has eligibility limits and runs to 15 Dec 2027.

falseAssumptions.claim: Rigid-frame towers reaching about 85% net-to-gross show that structural system is an efficiency lever at 244-305 m.
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat it as a sample correlation without height control; the tapered supertall sample found no significant system effect; leave the relationship unresolved until the STRC packet supplies plausible systems.

falseAssumptions.claim: The ACC credit reduces the negotiated CAC (or ACC) of a new rezoning.
falseAssumptions.correction: Credits are a transition rule for CAC rezonings secured before 30 Sep 2026. Default: ACC payable, no credit; netting in the CAC negotiation is a labelled scenario that never edits the ACC line.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Altus 2025 Vancouver concrete high-rise band ($360-455/sf) can be applied unchanged to 244-305 m towers.
falseAssumptions.correction: The band covers 13-39 storeys and hard cost only (no site servicing, consultants or development charges); apply a height-premium law and flag everything above 39 storeys as extrapolated.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Altus 2025 band ($360-455/sf) is a sufficient default hard cost for a downtown concrete residential tower.
falseAssumptions.correction: Show Altus 2025 and Coriolis 2026 ($580-630/sf gross buildable, downtown high-rise strata) side by side; the Coriolis range is 27-39% above the Altus top, unexplained pending scope definitions (parking, GFA basis).

falseAssumptions.claim: The Altus 2025 residential concrete band can serve as base hard cost for every use (office, hotel, retail, parking, transit link).
falseAssumptions.correction: Base cost is a per-use ledger: only residential concrete (13-39 storeys, $360-455/sf, hard cost only) is sourced by Altus; other uses stay blank or flagged team assumptions.

falseAssumptions.claim: The CAC share threshold (at least 75% of land lift) is a verified good outcome.
falseAssumptions.correction: It is an unverified secondary quote of policy 1.2(c); treat 75% as the City's legacy minimum target and display it as a reference, not a feasibility pass mark.

falseAssumptions.claim: The Metro Vancouver average asking rent of $31.20/sf in CBRE's Q2 2026 headline is the downtown office rent.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use class-matched downtown net asking rents: AAA $48.02, A $39.92, B $33.02, C $24.03 (all downtown classes $34.93).

falseAssumptions.claim: The P08 module graph has no cycles (r1 notes).
falseAssumptions.correction: M06 read the M05a cap rate and GDV while M05a reads M06. Cap rates moved to P08-M00, the public-use cost over GDV metric moved to M05b, and a validator compares each method's referenced outputs with depends_on.

falseAssumptions.claim: The height premium (N/N_ref)^eps anchored at N_ref = 26 (Altus band midpoint) is consistent with the Altus 13-39-storey band.
falseAssumptions.correction: Anchor at 39 storeys on the band top ($455/sf) and apply the premium only above 39 storeys; label 0.26 and 0.56 as lower bounds; show 2%/floor as linear (+42% at 60 storeys) and compound (+52%).

falseAssumptions.claim: UK PPG para 019 verifies a 15% profit-on-GDV threshold for this project.
falseAssumptions.correction: Status is team_assumption with a transferable benchmark: para 019 is plan-making guidance for England, allows alternative figures, and is not Vancouver practice or a site-specific test.

falseAssumptions.claim: Years to lease = new office GFA / downtown net absorption, with no competing vacancy.
falseAssumptions.correction: Years = (new rentable area + AAA+A vacancy above a structural rate) / (class-matched absorption x capture share); show AAA+A and all-class anchors and mark the anchor as two quarters only.

falseAssumptions.claim: Downtown Vancouver, or any Vancouver site, must provide a minimum number of off-street parking spaces.
falseAssumptions.correction: No minimum parking applies for any use citywide since 30 June 2024; the downtown peninsula was exempt from 2018. Accessible, visitor, bicycle and loading spaces are still required.

falseAssumptions.claim: FHWA Table 3-2 gives v/c bands of under 0.85 stable, 0.85-1.00 near capacity and over 1.00 oversaturated.
falseAssumptions.correction: Cite Table 3-2 exactly: under 0.85, 0.85-0.95 near capacity, 0.95-1.00 unstable flow, over 1.00 demand exceeds capacity. The single 0.85-1.00 band is from section 3.3.5. Add the reviewer-stated LOS F override for lane-group v/c above 1.0 (later HCM editions; unverified) and label the method HCM-style.

falseAssumptions.claim: For the neighbouring station, use the Expo trunk (2-3 min) and the Canada Line trunk (about 3 min) headways combined.
falseAssumptions.correction: Require a proxy-station choice and load only that station's lines from GTFS; combine trunks only at Waterfront; treat a new-station scenario as user-entered with per-line train capacity entered by the user.

falseAssumptions.claim: ITE trip rates do not consider location, so local survey data are the only option for downtown sites.
falseAssumptions.correction: ITE is paywalled but, per the reviewer, recent editions classify data by site setting (including Center City Core and Dense Multi-Use Urban) and report person trips; use as an optional cross-check where a user holds a licence.

falseAssumptions.claim: No cordon or screenline data exist, so auto occupancy, background volumes and truck shares are unsourced presets.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use TransLink screenline products as team-applied defaults: 2011 report (auto occupancy 1.24 regional, 1.17 AM peak, 1.25 CBD screenline; trucks about 6%), 2017 summary (trucks about 4%, CBD volume trend). They are vehicle counts at screenlines, through trips included, not site rates. The 2014 truck survey and 2023 screenline dashboard were not readable.

falseAssumptions.claim: On street footways, C+ (18 ppmm) is the fail line for every TfL area type, B- (15-17 ppmm) is only 'at risk', and B+ or better is the good level for every area type.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use the cell-level Figure 9 lookup by area type and by peak versus Average of Maximum, with the recommended minimum B+ (Figure 8) as the good line. C+ is the limit on a documented vitality exception (p.12), not the general fail line. Add the Tourist Attraction area type, the crossing-arm check (B- recommended, 15-18 ppmm) and the footway total-width minima (2.9, 4.2, 5.3 m).

falseAssumptions.claim: ParkingDemandEstimate = auto-driver commuters x occupancy.
falseAssumptions.correction: ParkingDemandEstimate = auto-driver vehicle arrivals x peak accumulation (default 1.0 is a labelled upper bound), with no occupancy multiplier. Apply occupancy only to a combined 'auto' share, selected by a driver_passenger_split flag on each mode-share row; unit tests cover both paths.

falseAssumptions.claim: Peak headways relevant to the station are Expo 2-5 min, Millennium 3-4 min and Canada 6 min.
falseAssumptions.correction: For a CBD station use the Expo trunk (about 2-3 min combined) and the Canada Line trunk (about 3 min combined), read from GTFS for the actual station. The Millennium Line terminates at VCC-Clark and is excluded.

falseAssumptions.claim: Published TDM reductions should be scaled down for a low-auto CBD site by k = site auto share / evidence auto share (capped at 1), so a CBD site gets a smaller claim.
falseAssumptions.correction: Select the evidence row by context (Ewing CBD and near-station columns, labelled as predictions). Keep k only as an optional sensitivity marked team assumption. Bound claims by an absolute floor at the lowest same-basis observed CBD share loaded in M01.

falseAssumptions.claim: Queue area per person of 1.4 m2 or more is Fruin LOS A-C and below 0.9 m2 is LOS E-F at stairs and fare lines.
falseAssumptions.correction: 1.4 and 0.9 m2 per person are walkway-scale boundaries (C/D and D/E). Queues use a separate queuing-area scale (reviewer: A 1.2 or more, B 0.9-1.2, C 0.7-0.9, D 0.3-0.7, E 0.2-0.3, F under 0.2 m2 per person). Keep both scales and cite the exhibit once read.

falseAssumptions.claim: TfL Figure 9 rates B 'at risk' at peak for Office and Retail, Residential and Transport Interchange, and rates B+ at risk and B unacceptable for Tourist Attraction (the previous critic's text-based reading, carried in r2 as an alternative to the geometry decode).
falseAssumptions.correction: Adopt the geometry decode and retire the alternative reading. Keep only the rendered-image confirmation by two people (31 Oct), and add an explicit rule that Figure 8 band C (21-23 ppmm), which Figure 9 omits (rows A, B+, B, B-, C+, C-, D, E), is read as the printed C- row.

falseAssumptions.claim: TfL Pedestrian Comfort Level bands are verified thresholds for peak-minute flows in below-grade station passages, with B+ (11 ppmm or less) good and 18 ppmm or more bad for all area types.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use TfL only for street footways and crossings, on peak-hour flow (people per hour / 60 / clear width), against the Figure 9 acceptability table by area type. Use station methods (TCQSM chapter 10 walkway and queuing scales) for passages, stairs and fare lines. Status: team_assumption.

falseAssumptions.claim: The 2014 Metro Vancouver Truck Classification and Dangerous Goods Survey is not readable because it exceeds the 10 MB fetch limit.
falseAssumptions.correction: A person reads it in the 7 Nov sprint for truck time-of-day profiles and light/heavy splits near the CBD and labels them 'screenline-type counts, not building rates'.

falseAssumptions.claim: The 2023 Trip Diary weekday shares for CBD sub-regions 21 and 22 are the right default mode split for all trips the tower generates (office, retail, hotel, residential).
falseAssumptions.correction: Use residence-based shares for residential trips and destination-based shares (trips ending in the CBD: Census place-of-work, City cordon counts or a dashboard destination filter) for attraction uses. Store basis, sample size and confidence interval with each loaded share and flag attraction runs on a residence-based share (r2: watermark, not block).

falseAssumptions.claim: The Trip Diary samples households by residence, so it cannot give workplace-attraction (destination-based) splits, and no destination-based Trip Diary product exists.
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat destination-end tabulation of the region-wide diary as valid, with caveats on geography, sample size, vintage and residents-only coverage. Load the 2008 Vancouver-CBD row as a candidate destination row and the 2011 Vancouver/UEL row once transcribed; test whether the 2023 dashboard filters by destination; keep Census place-of-work for CBD-scale commutes. The basis badge still flags a residence-end row used on an attraction.

falseAssumptions.claim: VTPI TDM reduction ranges (4-20%, about 15%, 34-37%, 35%) are verified thresholds for claimed reductions at a downtown Vancouver tower.
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat them as team-applied evidence ranges with an 'evidence context: US metro / predicted' label on each value.

falseAssumptions.claim: Any outrigger scheme is an unlisted SFRS with Rd = Ro = 1.0 (P10-M01).
falseAssumptions.correction: Core walls are the listed SFRS; outriggers and belts are capacity-protected elements; combined systems take the lowest RdRo (4.1.8.9(3)) or show equivalence (4.1.8.9(5)). Use three route states: listed + outrigger elements, equivalence, unlisted.

falseAssumptions.claim: CFD can replace wind-tunnel testing for specified wind loads or comfort.
falseAssumptions.correction: NBC 2020 Div B 4.1.7.1(6) states CFD shall not be used to determine specified wind loads; the Wind Tunnel Procedure is mandatory for very dynamically sensitive buildings (f1 <= 0.25 Hz, or occupied H/w > 6) and where wake buffeting is possible.

falseAssumptions.claim: Code empirical Ta can supply f1 for wind classification, and H/w <= 4 coloured green means no tunnel is needed (P10-M02).
falseAssumptions.correction: Ta is for seismic loads only. Use a dynamic-model f1; default tunnel_required = true for H >= about 180 m without one. Colour by the governing trigger.

falseAssumptions.claim: Core walls may be transferred or terminated at the podium if nonlinear dynamic analysis is done (P10-M01).
falseAssumptions.correction: NBC 4.1.8.10(4): where Ta >= 1.0 s and IE*S(1.0) > 0.25, non-wood SFRS shear walls run continuously from top to foundation with no Type 4 or 5 irregularity. Downtown X450 S(1.0) = 0.43 g and every 244-305 m tower has Ta > 1 s. Open podium spaces go around the core.

falseAssumptions.claim: Encapsulated mass timber in BC is limited to 12 storeys.
falseAssumptions.correction: BCBC 2024 Revision 1 and VBBL 2025 allow 18 storeys / 76 m with 70-minute encapsulation and area caps of 6,000 m2 (C) and 7,200 m2 (D, A-2); NBC 2020 itself remains at 12 storeys.

falseAssumptions.claim: Higher live load raises seismic weight W (P10-M08).
falseAssumptions.correction: W = dead load (partitions need not exceed 0.5 kPa) + 25% snow + 60% storage load + tank contents. Ordinary live load is excluded; wind-dynamics mass is a separate preset.

falseAssumptions.claim: Independent structural review is needed only when NLDA or an unlisted SFRS is used (P10-M03).
falseAssumptions.correction: Baseline documented independent review is always required in BC (EGBC bylaw quality-management standard); the Commentary J special-study panel (NLDA) and the City alternative-solution panel (unlisted) come on top.

falseAssumptions.claim: Mass-timber EMTC height is measured from the first-storey floor to the roof, and 'fire-separated parts' can be checked as separate buildings (P10-M06).
falseAssumptions.correction: Height runs to the uppermost floor level, excluding rooftop service enclosures. Only firewalls create separate buildings, so a timber podium joined to the tower is the same building.

falseAssumptions.claim: Modal-analysis seismic drifts can be compared directly with 0.025 hs (P10-M03).
falseAssumptions.correction: Elastic deflections including accidental torsion are multiplied by RdRo/IE (and by 1.2 for Type 9) before comparison with the limit; add Vd >= 0.8 V (regular) / 1.0 V (irregular).

falseAssumptions.claim: Moderately ductile concrete walls or steel braced frames can serve a tall Vancouver tower.
falseAssumptions.correction: At SC4 moderately ductile concrete shear/coupled walls are capped at 60 m and moderately ductile steel CBF or BRB at 40 m; only ductile walls, coupled walls, MRF, EBF and plate walls have no height limit.

falseAssumptions.claim: NBC 2020 ground motions already include Georgia-basin amplification.
falseAssumptions.correction: Commentary J states the NBC 2020 hazard model does not take basin effects into account and has no basin maps; UBC simulations indicate underestimation for tall shear-wall buildings.

falseAssumptions.claim: NBC wind serviceability limit is top drift <= H/500 under q50 = 0.45 kPa (P10-M01, P10-M08).
falseAssumptions.correction: Check total drift per storey <= hs/500 under service wind (Iw SLS = 0.75) with Dynamic Procedure pressures p = Iw q Ce Ct Cg Cp. Keep H/250-H/1000 only as Commentary I guidance.

falseAssumptions.claim: Outrigger, belt-truss, diagrid or mega-frame systems are code-listed SFRS with Rd and Ro values.
falseAssumptions.correction: No such SFRS appears in NBC 2020 Vol. 1 (text search); unlisted systems use Rd = Ro = 1.0 unless equivalence is proven by cyclic tests, NLDA, equivalent collapse margin and independent peer review; 'other' SFRS are not permitted at SC3-SC4.

falseAssumptions.claim: Stiff transfer floors acting as outriggers lengthen the real period versus the empirical formulas (P10-M01, P10-M05).
falseAssumptions.correction: Transfers or outrigger floors can shorten the real period below empirical Ta, so forces based on Ta may be unconservative. Flag the case for dynamic analysis.

falseAssumptions.claim: Strouhal number is about 1/5 for buildings (P10-M02, P10-M04).
falseAssumptions.correction: Use S = 1/7 for rectangular or polygonal plans and 1/5 only for circular plans; label non-circular results 'tunnel required' (para 105).

falseAssumptions.claim: The Commentary I worked example speeds (23.9 m/s) confirm the Vancouver Table C-2 column mapping (q10 = 0.34 kPa).
falseAssumptions.correction: q10 = 0.34 and q50 = 0.45 kPa are correct, but because they appear directly in the NBC 2020 Table C-2 Vancouver (City Hall) row, not because they match the example.

falseAssumptions.claim: The equivalent static method is adequate for a 244-305 m tower.
falseAssumptions.correction: It is permitted only for SC1-SC2, regular buildings under 60 m with Ta < 2 s, or irregular buildings under 20 m with Ta < 0.5 s; Vancouver is SC4, so dynamic analysis is required.

falseAssumptions.claim: Type 9 irregularity requires nonlinear dynamic analysis (P10-M01, P10-M03).
falseAssumptions.correction: NLDA with vertical motion is required only when alpha exceeds twice the Type 9 limit and IE*S(0.2) >= 0.5. Otherwise drift is multiplied by 1.2. Limits: alpha 0.1 (self-centering), 0.03 (other).

falseAssumptions.claim: Vancouver seismic design uses NBC 2015 / VBBL 2019 values (Sa(0.2) about 0.85 g, Class C).
falseAssumptions.correction: NBC 2020 X450 Sa(0.2) = 1.1 g (+25%) and Sa(2.0) = 0.27 g (+5%); VBBL 2025 seismic rules apply to new Vancouver projects from 15 Sep 2026 (in force on 21 Oct 2026); in-stream projects may use old rules until 8 Mar 2027.

falseAssumptions.claim: A 550 kPa plumbing pressure limit forces a plant floor, break tank or reducing station about every 56 m of height.
falseAssumptions.correction: The 550 kPa limit is handled by PRV stations per domestic-water zone. Plant-floor spacing follows hydronic equipment ratings, air-handling reach and riser congestion (editable presets). The 56 m figure is further corrected in an r2 flag.

falseAssumptions.claim: A single Table 10.2.2.5.A1 row (office, hotel or Group C) is the limit to test the tower's GHGI, TEUI and TEDI against.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use an area-weighted composite from M09 areas (method per City guidelines Section 5, unread), and offer Table B, Table C and the Passive House route as selectable paths.

falseAssumptions.claim: BC grid electricity is very low because 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh is its emission factor (and natural gas can be omitted from the factor table).
falseAssumptions.correction: 0.011 is the Part 9 prescriptive heating-source ceiling for EL-2 to EL-4, not a factor. Electricity and natural gas factors must come from the City Energy Modelling Guidelines; presets are unverified.

falseAssumptions.claim: BCBC 2024, with its adaptable-unit rule from 10 March 2025 and the provincial Zero Carbon and Energy Step Codes, is the confirmed governing code for the Vancouver site, and these thresholds are verified.
falseAssumptions.correction: VBBL 2025 (By-law 14343, in force 15 September 2025, base text BCBC 2024 as amended) governs. Provincial-only rules are shown as reference with Vancouver applicability unverified.

falseAssumptions.claim: CIBSE Guide D (2015) provides the current lift-design criteria.
falseAssumptions.correction: The 2015 edition is archived and superseded by the 2020 edition; 2025 sections are listed as in preparation.

falseAssumptions.claim: Canadian and Vancouver codes require refuge floors (as in some Asian jurisdictions) in supertall towers.
falseAssumptions.correction: No refuge-floor clause appears among the Subsection 3.2.6 requirements listed in the 2024 BC Part 3 checklists (smoke movement, emergency elevator operation, firefighter elevator, venting, central alarm and control facility, voice communication). Treat refuge or waiting areas as design choices or alternative-solution arguments.

falseAssumptions.claim: Emergency crossover access (3.4.6.18) is a different provision from stair re-entry doors (r1 text cited VBBL 2007 3.4.6.17 for re-entry).
falseAssumptions.correction: In VBBL 2019, 3.4.6.18 'Emergency Crossover Access to Floor Areas' is the re-entry rule; 3.4.6.17 is 'Security for Banks and Mercantile Floor Areas'. Stair doors may not lock against entry where travel to an unlocked door exceeds 2 storeys.

falseAssumptions.claim: No refuge-type provision exists, so any refuge or waiting area is purely a design choice.
falseAssumptions.correction: Keep 'no mandatory refuge floor'. r1 added 3.3.1.7 protected zones to the checklist; r2 note: 3.3.1.7 is deleted in Vancouver, so see the r2 flag. Keep an evacuation-elevator item.

falseAssumptions.claim: One person per 8 m2 NIA is one of the sourced design densities on an equal footing.
falseAssumptions.correction: 1 per 8 is a London speculative buffer; the developer expected about 1 per 10 on average. Default office density is 1 per 10 m2 as a team assumption, with 1 per 8 as an option.

falseAssumptions.claim: Passenger-shaft area is the lift core area, so NetToGross computed from it is meaningful.
falseAssumptions.correction: Total core adds firefighter, stretcher, goods and parking lifts, lobbies, pits and overruns. Passenger-only and total are reported separately and net-to-gross uses the total.

falseAssumptions.claim: Protected zones in accessible floor areas (3.3.1.7) are a current checklist item for this tower, typically met by sprinklers.
falseAssumptions.correction: Vancouver deletes the article. Mark it 'deleted in VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019, confirm VBBL 2025', make the metric information only, and keep refuge or assisted-evacuation areas as alternative-solution options tied to P11-M08.

falseAssumptions.claim: RTT = 2H*tv + (S+1)*ts + 2P*tp is the general-analysis form used in P11-S23, and is valid for every rise of a supertall.
falseAssumptions.correction: P11-S23 prints no such equation. The formula is the classic equal-floor form with no express-jump term and P undefined. The engine uses general analysis with a kinematic express term and P = average car load.

falseAssumptions.claim: Residential and hotel lift population can be derived from area / density.
falseAssumptions.correction: Residential and hotel population uses persons per dwelling by bedroom count or per room with occupancy rate; area-based density applies to offices only.

falseAssumptions.claim: Sprinkler status can be switched off per storey as a legitimate option for a 244-305 m tower.
falseAssumptions.correction: Lock sprinklers to 'required' (NFPA 13); an 'off' entry is only a flagged alternative solution.

falseAssumptions.claim: The 1% contaminated air over 2 h stair target is only a design target from BCAB 1844's facts, not a code limit, and it applies to the tower's exit stairs.
falseAssumptions.correction: It is a code performance requirement, Sentence 3.2.6.2.(2), for exit stairs serving storeys below the lowest exit level (including transit-link levels), at the January 2.5% design temperature. Stairs above get the bottom vent (0.05 m2 per door, minimum 1.8 m2).

falseAssumptions.claim: The Vancouver January 2.5% design temperature for 3.2.6.2.(2) has not been retrieved and must be a user entry.
falseAssumptions.correction: Preset -6 C (1% = -8 C) from VBBL 2019 Table C-2; future rows -4 C (2020s) and -2 C (2050s). Re-check VBBL 2025.

falseAssumptions.claim: The domestic-water pressure zone height is 550 kPa / 9.81 kPa per m, about 56 m.
falseAssumptions.correction: Zone height = (P_max - P_min_residual) / 9.81 for downfeed zones, with a branch-PRV option limited by pipe and valve ratings. Cite VPBL 2019 Book II 2.6.3.3, check VBBL 2025 Book II.

falseAssumptions.claim: The high-building ruler needs both an 18 m and a 36 m trigger line, because the NBC 36 m rule might apply to Groups A, D, E and F.
falseAssumptions.correction: Draw only the 18 m Vancouver line; keep the 36 m NBC rule in the edition map.

falseAssumptions.claim: The maximum travel distance for each occupancy is set in 3.4.2.4.
falseAssumptions.correction: Limit values sit in 3.4.2.5 (location of exits); 3.4.2.4 covers measurement and the 50 m service-space case; 3.3.1.6 covers travel within suites. The sprinkler switch selects the limit.

falseAssumptions.claim: VBBL 2007 is the most recent Vancouver Part 3 text that can be read, so its values are the presets.
falseAssumptions.correction: Re-stamp presets to VBBL 2019 (Part 3 to 1 Jul 2024; Section 3.5 to 1 Jan 2021; Section 3.8 to 7 Mar 2023) and download VBBL 2025 by hand. VBBL 2007 stays in the edition map only.

falseAssumptions.claim: Vancouver's rules on adaptable units, power door operators, tactile indicators and accessible hotel rooms are unknown, so only provincial BCBC 2024 references can be shown.
falseAssumptions.correction: Base M07 on VBBL 2019 Section 3.8: 3.8.5.1 adaptable units, 3.8.2.7 power doors, 3.8.2.10 tactile indicators, 3.8.2.12 hotel rooms (1 per 40, plus 1 per 20 with visual alarm). Show provincial rules only as comparison.

falseAssumptions.claim: A net-to-gross factor can be applied to DOE/PNNL densities and the energy 'design' population can size lifts.
falseAssumptions.correction: PNNL densities are per zone floor area, so efficiency applies only to net-basis densities. Lifts use their own vertical-transportation basis; egress uses the VBBL table and 2 persons per sleeping area, not DOE 2.5 per unit.

falseAssumptions.claim: A visibility-graph partition can have fractional transparency (0 to 1).
falseAssumptions.correction: A visibility edge exists or not. Use binary flags (opaque, glazed, open) and two graphs: visibility at eye height, accessibility at floor height with glass as a barrier, as Turner et al. built for the Barcelona Pavilion.

falseAssumptions.claim: An A1-A3 embodied-carbon sum can be tested pass/fail against Vancouver's 800 kgCO2e/m2 cap.
falseAssumptions.correction: 800 is the City's 2023 absolute limit over stages A-C (60 years) for structure and shell, so an A1-A3 sum is a partial scope. A 10% reduction (360 absolute) was proposed for 2025; adoption is unconfirmed. Show scope-labelled reference lines, no badge.

falseAssumptions.claim: BC 25 MPa concrete ranges from 220 to 90 kgCO2e/m3 (like-for-like), and CLF BC guide values can be used as open data.
falseAssumptions.correction: The 90 figure is a 91-day EPD and the 220 baseline is at 28 days; compare Butler 109 (28 d) with 220. The guide carries an all-rights-reserved notice and no licence, so link to it and do not bundle its values.

falseAssumptions.claim: BC Building Code 2024 (occupant loads, separations, acoustics) and the BC Energy Step Code govern a tower in downtown Vancouver.
falseAssumptions.correction: The City of Vancouver has its own building by-law. Use the Vancouver Building By-law (2025 edition, in force from 15 Sep 2025 per City guide snippets) and the City's energy and emissions metrics (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI); VBBL 2019 s.10.2 values are now read (see r2 flag), VBBL 2025 values unverified.

falseAssumptions.claim: CLF Material Baselines are CC BY 4.0 and can ship as open data in the tool.
falseAssumptions.correction: Only the 2023 v2 report states CC BY 4.0. The 2025 report and the 2026 dataset are CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike): bundled or derived data must carry the same licence. Ship 2023 values with attribution, or isolate 2025/2026 data as a separate CC BY-SA package.

falseAssumptions.claim: Competition entrants can record Indigenous consultation status as obtained or in progress.
falseAssumptions.correction: Entrants are anonymous, have weeks and no relationship with the Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh Nations. The fixed status is 'no consultation possible in this exercise'; motif generation is blocked and items go to CULT as 'not proposed'.

falseAssumptions.claim: EN 17037 view-out levels are an area-share criterion ('% of area by EN 17037 level').
falseAssumptions.correction: The standard's view-out methods are point-in-space assessments (Annex C). Report per-point levels; the area share is a ClimateStudio-style convention and is labelled so.

falseAssumptions.claim: Embodied carbon per material can come from EC3 and ICE in the open-source tool.
falseAssumptions.correction: ICE Database Educational V5.0 (June 2026) is educational-only; software, tools, reporting and project calculations are excluded and non-educational use is no longer permitted from 30 Sept 2026. Use EC3/openEPD EPDs and CLF baselines (CC BY 4.0) in the tool; ICE only as user-supplied data in a teaching mode.

falseAssumptions.claim: LEED v4/v4.1 credit thresholds (EQc7 sDA/ASE, EQc8 views) are the current LEED benchmark.
falseAssumptions.correction: LEED v5 (April 2025 launch edition) is available for BD+C. Label v4 and v4.1 values legacy_version; v5 values come from a secondary page (LEEDuser) and stay unverified until the USGBC text is opened.

falseAssumptions.claim: No source resolves how bird-friendly patterned glass and LEED view glazing can both be satisfied.
falseAssumptions.correction: CaGBC says the LEED v4.1 addenda clarified frit and pattern wording to align with bird-collision deterrence; the LEEDuser v5 page says frits, patterns or tints must preserve the view. Only the VLT and view-clarity trade-off remains, as a judgement.

falseAssumptions.claim: The ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix G baseline WWR (office 40%, hotel 34%) is a limit that a facade must stay under.
falseAssumptions.correction: It is the reference model's WWR used for performance comparison. Show 40% and 34% only as reference lines (proxy) and judge the facade by the ENER result against the City's TEDI, TEUI and GHGI.

falseAssumptions.claim: The LEEDuser v5 EQc2 page is internally inconsistent on Option 5 points.
falseAssumptions.correction: Re-read r2: Option 5 Path 3 (proximity to windows) is 1 point; Path 4 (sDA) is 1-4 points at 40/55/65/75%; views are Option 1 Path 2 (2-3 points). The page stays a secondary source; USGBC text unopened.

falseAssumptions.claim: Turner et al. (2001) report only qualitative correspondence between visibility-graph measures and use.
falseAssumptions.correction: The paper reports an exponential fit (R2 = 0.63) between observed Tate Gallery room occupancy and mean shortest path length. It is evidence for relative use in one building, not a threshold.

falseAssumptions.claim: UBC bird-friendly policy has Tiers 1-3, with 55% treated glazing (Tier 3) the lowest level.
falseAssumptions.correction: Table 1 lists four tiers: 90%, 85% and 55% treated up to 16 m or 4 m above the tallest vegetation, and Tier 4 with no percentage. Tiers 1-2 add all glazing next to vegetation or water; Tier 3 large areas; Tier 4 glazing near habitat or migratory paths. All tiers: no fly-through, corners 5 m, Dark Sky lighting.

falseAssumptions.claim: VBBL energy and emissions limits (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI) by occupancy could not be read, so ENER results show without a limit line.
falseAssumptions.correction: Table 10.2.2.5.A1 is readable in the open BC Publications VBBL 2019 consolidation: Group C over 6 storeys 120/30/3.0; hotel and motel 140/20/4.0; office 100/20/3.0; Group D and E except office 120/20/3.0; other occupancies GHGI 50% below a fossil-fuel reference. Show as legacy_version lines, occupancy-weighted, no badge.

falseAssumptions.claim: Vancouver's older view-cone policy with 38 cones, including Queen Elizabeth Park cones 3.1 and 3.2.4a, is still in force.
falseAssumptions.correction: On 10 July 2024 Council repealed it and adopted Public Views Guidelines with 24 cones; Queen Elizabeth Park 3.2.1-3.2.4 remain, 3.1 and 3.2.4a were removed. The Higher Buildings Policy Review says protected views are not being reviewed.

falseAssumptions.claim: 21 Oct to 13 Nov offers 18 working days (36 person-days), enough for the 29-34 person-day core.
falseAssumptions.correction: 11 Nov (Remembrance Day, BC statutory holiday) leaves 17 working days = 34 person-days at full time for two students (13 days to 6 Nov, 15 to 10 Nov). Core is re-planned validator-first: about 28 person-days plus 15% reserve = 32; it fits only at an availability factor of about 0.95, so M02 v0 and the M05 route are first to slip.

falseAssumptions.claim: A tower top above the Queen Elizabeth Park view-cone ceiling is 'bad' (P13-M03 metric).
falseAssumptions.correction: Report encroachment neutrally (height above or below the ceiling, encroached area per cone, angular share) and require a breach-register rationale; only 'encroachment without rationale' or 'ceiling unknown' is amber, never red.

falseAssumptions.claim: Ask the Jury gives one free question per registration for VTC, so the brief question on Nation names uses that slot (qa_question_budget; Q&A pack Q1).
falseAssumptions.correction: Send Q1 and C1-C9 to the organiser contact (C8 and C9 by Fri 23 Oct, the rest by Fri 30 Oct, before the 3 Nov close). Use Ask the Jury only if the portal shows it after registration and log that observation; qa_question_budget reads portal_observations, with null meaning organiser contact.

falseAssumptions.claim: Boards can be delivered as PDF (implied by the scope line 'export (PDF/JPG)').
falseAssumptions.correction: Each panel must be a JPEG (.jpg/.jpeg) of at most 10 MB; PDF is useful only as a team proof.

falseAssumptions.claim: Closing at 23:59 London time on 30 Nov 2026 equals 15:59 Vancouver (PST); the earlier flag on 'end of day Vancouver' gave this conversion as its correction.
falseAssumptions.correction: 23:59 London (GMT) on 30 Nov 2026 = 2026-11-30T23:59Z = 16:59 Vancouver (UTC-7). Store the UTC instant, use the earlier of 23:59 (page) and 24.00 (Terms 4.7), and check at runtime that the Intl offset for America/Vancouver parses to -420 minutes, with a fixed-offset fallback.

falseAssumptions.claim: Entrant eligibility needs no check beyond identity verification and team size (gates G-01, G-02).
falseAssumptions.correction: Add gate G-00 (every member's attestation to Terms 3.3.1-3.3.5 plus a logged written organiser answer to C8, sent before fees are paid); G-04 also blocks any board-linked asset shown to a listed juror, including in course reviews.

falseAssumptions.claim: Hidden lines can be obtained as 'all projected edges minus visible' with a clipper2-js difference.
falseAssumptions.correction: Clip projected edges against the polygons of nearer occluding faces, or subtract collinear visible sub-segments from each edge by parameter intervals with a tolerance; keep the hidden class Make2D-only until a pilot comparison passes.

falseAssumptions.claim: Number of panels (4), number of ground-level perspectives (>= 4) and the landscape A2 rule are 'verified'.
falseAssumptions.correction: Status is unverified (transcribed from the brief by the team) until the brief PDF is stored with a SHA-256 and two members check the transcription; panel count is modelled as a brief_register value (exact or maximum), default exact 4. Only the upper bound of four (Terms 4.8) and A2 = 420 x 594 mm (ISO 216) are verified.

falseAssumptions.claim: Only the Queen Elizabeth Park cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 matter for a downtown tower's protected-view check.
falseAssumptions.correction: Intersect the site and tower footprints with all 24 cones for the declared site_georeference, report every intersecting cone neutrally (view_number, name, overlap, ceiling or unknown, angular share) and re-run under a one-block shift.

falseAssumptions.claim: Rhino Make2D supplies the hidden-line layers (cited as P13-S30), so the browser route can offer a hidden-line class.
falseAssumptions.correction: Cite P13-S27 for Make2D. The browser route offers cut, silhouette, crease and visible classes; hidden lines come from imported Make2D output or a prototype hidden-line pass, marked untested.

falseAssumptions.claim: The 30 Nov 2026 deadline is end of day in Vancouver.
falseAssumptions.correction: Closing is 23:59 London time on 30 Nov 2026 and the tracker shows both time zones. [SUPERSEDED: the '15:59 Vancouver (PST)' conversion first written here is wrong; the correct value is 16:59 Vancouver (UTC-7), see the next flag.]

falseAssumptions.claim: The Vancouver offset check compares the Intl 'longOffset' output with the string '-07:00'.
falseAssumptions.correction: Parse the timeZoneName part of formatToParts: strip 'GMT' (an empty remainder means +00:00), convert to minutes and compare with -420.

falseAssumptions.claim: The brief PDF 'could not be opened here', so board count, A2 landscape, jury weights and the 20 items must stay unverified and the 6 Nov validator can ship without them.
falseAssumptions.correction: The team holds the PDF (the project description states its brief facts come from it). Only the spec authors' fetch tool could not reach it. By 23-24 Oct the team stores the PDF in the repo, records its SHA-256 and two members transcribe the rules with page numbers into brief_register; the statuses then flip to verified. The 6 Nov validator does not ship with an empty register.

falseAssumptions.claim: The exact Queen Elizabeth Park view-cone origin and azimuth cannot be obtained because City of Vancouver hosts returned 403.
falseAssumptions.correction: Derive the origin and azimuths of cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 from the City Open Data 'View cones' dataset: shared apex near 49.24216 N, 123.11244 W; bearings 341.4 to 19.5 degrees; lengths 5.50-6.20 km (computed). Only ceiling heights remain unverified, and apex-as-designated-origin stays an inference until the Public Views Guidelines are read.

falseAssumptions.claim: The gpt-image-2.5 models are not on OpenAI's zero-data-retention list (P13-M05 data_retention, S54, the earlier OpenAI UNVERIFIED flag).
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat gpt-image-2.5-sunburst and gpt-image-2.5-flare as ZDR-eligible, with the 30-day default retention unless ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring is actually enabled. Log per ledger row which setting is in force.

falseAssumptions.claim: A 1 degree true-north error moves a shadow tip about 1.7 m, which justifies a 0.5 degree target
falseAssumptions.correction: Tolerance restated as good <= 0.25 degree, bad >= 1 degree (team assumption that depends on the CLIM packets).

falseAssumptions.claim: A local Z = 0 at the entrance floor sidesteps vertical datum mixing
falseAssumptions.correction: Z0 geodetic elevation and vertical datum are required georeference fields, defaulted from LiDAR ground at the entrance and confirmed by the user, exported as IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight and IfcProjectedCRS.VerticalDatum. EPSG:3157 itself has no vertical axis (P14-S57).

falseAssumptions.claim: City of Vancouver building footprints and heights can serve as a current context model
falseAssumptions.correction: The dataset 'Building footprints 2009' is derived from 2009 LiDAR, 'approximate, best used for comparison' and 'not being updated'. Use LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2) or the organiser's 3D model for current heights.

falseAssumptions.claim: EPSG:26910 (proj4 +datum=NAD83) is the right CRS for City of Vancouver data, and mixing it with WGS84 shifts positions 2-4 m
falseAssumptions.correction: Project CRS is EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N. EPSG lists the CSRS-to-WGS84 transformation accuracy as 1.0 m (alternative 2.0 m); EPSG:26910 stays an accepted import alias with a warning. See the r2 flag on how the 3157 definition must be registered.

falseAssumptions.claim: EPSG:3157 can be registered in proj4js directly from the epsg.io PROJ string
falseAssumptions.correction: Register +towgs84=-0.991,1.9072,0.5129,0.025790,0.009650,0.011660,0 (arc-seconds, position-vector sign, derived) or a null shift for City-to-City data, chosen by a LiDAR frame test, and unit-test both against PROJ to under 1 cm. Parcel agreement restated at 0.3 m good and 1.0 m bad.

falseAssumptions.claim: Every ProgramVolume can be sliced into floor plates at every storey elevation without distorting area
falseAssumptions.correction: Add a per-volume floors-present list and FloorPlate.has_floor; count only floored plates in gross and counted FSR area, list void area apart, and map mezzanines to PARTIAL storeys.

falseAssumptions.claim: Extrusion and SubD mesh access in rhino3dm is unconfirmed, and no Extrusion binding file exists
falseAssumptions.correction: Add a deterministic fallback mesher: exact prism for polyline-profile extrusions, earcut triangulation of planar Brep faces, SubD control net labelled 'volume biased', and a Rhino export how-to for the rest; block on unmeshed ProgramVolumes.

falseAssumptions.claim: No source gives the downtown street-grid skew
falseAssumptions.correction: Show the skew as a derived value (default 44.7 and 134.7 deg), keep it separate from UTM grid convergence (about 0.09 deg), and use it for an independent street-edge check of the true-north rotation. Which north the organiser's arrow shows stays unresolved.

falseAssumptions.claim: Rhino.Compute is not available to Educational licences (in general)
falseAssumptions.correction: Narrow the claim to what the page says; record workstation licensing as unverified.

falseAssumptions.claim: Speckle keys objects by applicationId (cited to the pre-2026.9 data-schema page)
falseAssumptions.correction: Store IFC GlobalId, source applicationId, Layer 0 UUID and our own SHA-256 separately; cite P14-S10 for the 2026.9 model and treat P14-S09 as historical.

falseAssumptions.claim: Speckle server and SDKs are licensed Apache-2.0
falseAssumptions.correction: Record 'Apache-2.0 except EE modules (workspaces, gatekeeper)'; a self-hosted server either leaves those directories out or accepts the EE terms (whether it runs without them is undocumented in the pages read); cite each connector repository for its own licence; the CI licence audit in P14-M07 checks every licence column.

falseAssumptions.claim: The direction of IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure between zone and spaces is unconfirmed
falseAssumptions.correction: IfcSpatialZone is the RelatingStructure and its IfcSpaces the RelatedElements; reference each zone from its IfcBuilding too, and add bot:containsZone from the zone to its plates. Only the IFC4 ADD2 pages remain to confirm in the round-trip spike.

falseAssumptions.claim: The ground-to-grid scale factor can be stored in IfcMapConversion.Scale
falseAssumptions.correction: Keep Scale = 1.0 in the IFC4 ADD2 export; store the grid factor in Layer 0 and a custom pset; use IfcMapConversionScaled with a Z factor of 1 for IFC4X3.

falseAssumptions.claim: The meaning of avght_m, maxht_m and the datum of topelev_m in Building footprints 2009 is undocumented
falseAssumptions.correction: Field meanings moved to resolved (use maxht_m only for building-level summaries); the name of the vertical datum behind topelev_m stays unresolved. (r3: the maxht_m wording proved unreliable, see the r3 flag.)

falseAssumptions.claim: The north-type enum 'true, grid or magnetic' is unambiguous for a Vancouver designer
falseAssumptions.correction: Four plain-language types with a diagram: true north, magnetic north (about 15.4 degrees east, derived), projection (UTM) grid north, street-grid (plan) north.

falseAssumptions.claim: The rhino3dm fallback mesher can triangulate planar Brep faces 'from edge loops with earcut'
falseAssumptions.correction: Rebuild loops from face.duplicateFace(false) edges: sample each edge (pointAtStart, pointAtEnd, pointAt, isLinear), chain by endpoint within the file's absolute tolerance, project with the planar surface's frameAt, take the largest absolute signed area as the outer loop, run earcut and the area check, then weld vertices across faces and test with manifold-3d (Mesh.merge, status). Add a CI fixture: a BooleanUnion polysurface saved without render meshes. Unverified until that fixture passes.

falseAssumptions.claim: The true-north error can be checked by comparing the arrow-derived bearing with a 'confirmed true north'
falseAssumptions.correction: Check instead that the site's street-facing edges align with the parcel-derived street bearings after the chosen rotation (good <= 0.25 degree, bad >= 1 degree), and report the arrow-to-street angle (about 44.7 deg for a true or UTM-grid arrow, about 29.3 deg for a magnetic one).

falseAssumptions.claim: The wasm32 4 GiB memory ceiling is the browser limit for imports
falseAssumptions.correction: Use each WASM module's declared maximum memory as the limit (good <= 50%, bad >= 80%) and treat Safari as the constraining browser.

falseAssumptions.claim: Tower height (244-305 m) threshold status is 'verified'
falseAssumptions.correction: Status corrected; the range is unverified until the brief PDF is read, and the height is shown under three conventions in P14-M05.

falseAssumptions.claim: Tower-height metric status 'false_assumption_corrected' reflects the evidence
falseAssumptions.correction: Status 'unverified'; the earlier wrong 'verified' label stays logged as the r1 FALSE ASSUMPTION flag above.

falseAssumptions.claim: maxht_m of a footprint can be compared with a tower's published height (r2: 208.6 m against 201 m)
falseAssumptions.correction: Compare part topelev_m minus baseelev_m (hgt_agl) with the CTBUH label: 192.95 m against 201 m is -4.0% and 141.22 m against 147 m is -3.9% (position-only match). The tallest part within 2.5 km is 192.95 m (top 223.71 m geodetic), still below the 244-305 m class. Keep maxht_m as a flagged summary only.

falseAssumptions.claim: web-ifc benchmark: 29-70 MB files open in 0.45-1.2 s and mesh in 4.6-7.6 s
falseAssumptions.correction: Quote the full range (open 0.17-1.16 s, execute 0.52-7.6 s for 26-70 MB) and set thresholds from our own measurement of a VTC-sized model on a mid-range Windows laptop.

falseAssumptions.claim: A Web Worker created by our page inherits the page's Content-Security-Policy and is therefore a safe place for community code.
falseAssumptions.correction: Workers are generally not governed by the creating document's CSP; a worker script must be served with its own CSP header (blob: and data: workers inherit). Workers also still have network access unless blocked.

falseAssumptions.claim: A keyboard alternative satisfies the drag requirement ('Single-pointer or keyboard alternative to drag', WCAG 2.5.7).
falseAssumptions.correction: Provide single-pointer, non-drag alternatives (click source then target, select then nudge or click destination, numeric size fields) and test keyboard operability separately under SC 2.1.1.

falseAssumptions.claim: A sandboxed community worker can carry its own CSP response header (connect-src none) inside an opaque-origin iframe, with the sandbox hosted on GitHub Pages.
falseAssumptions.correction: Put the CSP and the sandbox directive on the sandbox iframe document's response header, on a header-capable separate domain; the blob worker inherits it. Test denial of fetch, WebSocket, importScripts, nested Worker, eval and top navigation in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

falseAssumptions.claim: About 3 dev-weeks of capacity are available for P15 core before 13 Nov (r2 schedule flag).
falseAssumptions.correction: P14 core is 21.0 person-days (62% of nominal 34 to 13 Nov; its 19.5 slice is 75% of 26 to 6 Nov). P15 core is re-baselined to 12.0 person-days (never-cut minimum 7.0); 21.0 + 12.0 = 33.0 of 34 before P13 and P16 are counted.

falseAssumptions.claim: Connect, move and resize are the drag actions needing single-pointer alternatives (M01 SC 2.5.7 metric).
falseAssumptions.correction: Inventory all drag props: pan, edge reconnect, marquee and minimap pan too; give each a click alternative or disable it, and test by enumerating enabled props.

falseAssumptions.claim: INP thresholds are 'verified' for measuring canvas interaction latency in a test build at the 75th percentile.
falseAssumptions.correction: Reclassified as team_assumption. Use a scripted interaction set and report Event Timing p98 per session, with Total Blocking Time as a secondary lab proxy.

falseAssumptions.claim: Incremental re-run bands (good <= 5 s, bad > 30 s) have no sourced benchmark (M02).
falseAssumptions.correction: Rebase on Nielsen's limits: good <= 1 s for T0 and formula nodes, acceptable <= 10 s, bad > 10 s unless a percent-done indicator and Cancel are shown; a sourced guideline applied by our reading.

falseAssumptions.claim: Longest-list matching is design logic supported by P15-S12.
falseAssumptions.correction: Cite McNeel's data-stream-matching page (P15-S90) for the documented default, stamp repeated items, offer strict matching for metric nodes. r3: that page is a 2020 Explicit History labs page, so Grasshopper's own default stays unverified.

falseAssumptions.claim: Pyodide/WebAssembly isolation is enough to run untrusted community Python safely in the browser.
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat Pyodide as one layer only. A 7 Aug 2026 disclosure showed escapes in seven products (ctypes and Emscripten exports reached the JS host). Add host-level isolation (separate origin, CSP on the sandbox document, no network), allowlists, stripped exports, maintainer review, or run server-side in a sandbox.

falseAssumptions.claim: Scripting a drag and recording Event Timing durations measures canvas drag latency (M01, M02 and M04 latency metrics).
falseAssumptions.correction: Use Event Timing (durationThreshold 16 ms) only for discrete interactions, p98 over all scripted interactions with unreported ones counted as 16 ms. Measure drag, pan and zoom as frame times.

falseAssumptions.claim: Setting selectionOnDrag off removes marquee drag, and shift-click can serve as the multi-select alternative.
falseAssumptions.correction: Set selectionKeyCode to null (default 'Shift' still draws a selection box) and use outline checkboxes; the default multi-select key is Control or Meta, not Shift. Add pinch (SC 2.5.1) with Controls zoom buttons.

falseAssumptions.claim: Storing a named actor with every decided_by value is harmless to VTC anonymity.
falseAssumptions.correction: Actors are local pseudonyms (member-A); the name map stays on the device and is excluded from every exporter; RunRecord and graph JSON join the scan scope; environment blocks omit user, host and path.

falseAssumptions.claim: T0 declarative modules need no code execution and are therefore safe before the sandbox ships.
falseAssumptions.correction: T0 expressions arrive in imported JSON, so the evaluator is attack surface: allow-list grammar, caps, worker with deadline, Ajv-validated imports without prototype keys, fuzz suite. mathjs is dropped from core.

falseAssumptions.claim: The SemVer compliance metric (MINOR inside 0.y.z counts as breaking) is 'verified', and other policy thresholds (licence field OSI rule, CI gate, SemVer detection, community profile, pointer target size) were verified.
falseAssumptions.correction: Relabelled team_assumption with the verified part kept in the basis: SemVer item 4 says only that 0.y.z may change; the MINOR rule is the node-semver caret convention.

falseAssumptions.claim: The VTC terms say nothing that restricts redistribution of competition materials, and only anonymity constrains entrants' publishing.
falseAssumptions.correction: Never host Buildner's Presentation Template Package in modules or templates. Treat sharing design visuals before judging as a risk under 4.1, and keep projects local by default.

falseAssumptions.claim: The core export flow strips author, team and path metadata using the listed library (exifr).
falseAssumptions.correction: exifr only reads. Core uses a first-party lossless allow-list JPEG segment rewriter, a re-scan, a size check and a stamp bound to the post-strip hash. PDF leaves core (VTC panels are JPEG).

falseAssumptions.claim: Two of the seven products in the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure received no fix.
falseAssumptions.correction: Four of seven (cohere-terrarium, langchain-sandbox, stlite, cibuildwheel) had no code fix; the three fixes that shipped (n8n external runners, Grist Deno, smolagents removing WasmExecutor) moved or removed in-process Pyodide. Make T3 the Python default and keep browser Pyodide as a dev tier.

falseAssumptions.claim: Whether giscus needs a public repository is unknown.
falseAssumptions.correction: giscus requires a public repository with the giscus app installed and Discussions enabled, so all comments are public and tied to GitHub accounts; module-page threads only, with a privacy notice.

falseAssumptions.claim: litegraph.js (or its Comfy fork) is a maintained, safe choice for the node canvas.
falseAssumptions.correction: Original litegraph.js last pushed 2024-08-01 with about 1.2 k weekly downloads; the Comfy-Org fork is archived (2026-01-14). Use @xyflow/react (pushed 2026-10-20, about 8.3 M weekly downloads) with Rete as the fallback.

falseAssumptions.claim: npm provenance provides signed provenance for registry module bundles.
falseAssumptions.correction: Use GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest) on bundle files, verify them in CI with gh attestation verify, and have the client check the index SHA-256; mirror accepted bundles.

falseAssumptions.claim: A capability token with its own budget, a task allow-list and no key access means a malicious community fork cannot send raw geometry out.
falseAssumptions.correction: State module isolation as a goal until built and tested: sandboxed iframe without allow-same-origin on a separate origin, CSP default-src 'none', connect-src 'none', form-action 'none', typed message ports, summarised inputs, and a planted-module exfiltration control case that must fail closed. Community-module upload stays off until it passes.

falseAssumptions.claim: An exact-string match of the stored quote in the source text resolves an anchor (100% resolution target).
falseAssumptions.correction: Count a quote as resolved only when exact+prefix+suffix gives exactly one match inside the expected clause; report unique, ambiguous and unmatched separately.

falseAssumptions.claim: Claude Code can call OpenAI by running the OpenAI Codex CLI as an MCP server (`codex mcp-server`).
falseAssumptions.correction: The codex mcp-server command and binary have been removed; the replacement app server uses JSON-RPC, not MCP, and is experimental. Use openai/codex-plugin-cc, `codex exec` via Bash, or the read-only Docs MCP.

falseAssumptions.claim: Credential variables are not expanded in remote URLs or headers of project-scoped MCP servers (P16-M07).
falseAssumptions.correction: Treat ${OPENAI_API_KEY} or ${CODEX_API_KEY} in .mcp.json as live secrets that may be sent. Keep secret-bearing remote servers out of project scope, start CI and -p runs with --strict-mcp-config, put .mcp.json and .claude/** under CODEOWNERS, and test with a planted .mcp.json.

falseAssumptions.claim: Exceeding the Higher Buildings Policy 'may be considered' 600 ft (183 m) height is discretionary and returns 'needs justification', not a breach.
falseAssumptions.correction: Below 183 m: Permission. Above: the tower exceeds the policy's height limits, so record a justified-departure item. Whether the VTC site lies inside the policy area stays UNRESOLVED; the derived limit card (Prohibition, defeasible) stays UNVERIFIED until the policy text is read.

falseAssumptions.claim: LLM cost per call is input plus cache plus a small fixed output (500 tokens for cited QA; 100 for an entailment check on Haiku 5.5), so a cited answer costs about $0.02-$0.05.
falseAssumptions.correction: Model thinking and reasoning tokens explicitly, fix effort per cached conversation, record thinking_tokens and reasoning_tokens, reserve the max_tokens worst case, and show cost limits as UNVERIFIED until a ~20-call pilot per route. Assumed thinking of 1,000-5,000 tokens per call moves the 40-case suite from $13.26 to $23.43-$60.66.

falseAssumptions.claim: LegalRuleML strict / defeasible / defeater correspond to deontic strength shall / should / may.
falseAssumptions.correction: Keep two card fields: deontic_type (obligation, prohibition, permission, right) and strength (strict, defeasible, defeater).

falseAssumptions.claim: OpenAI file_search citations (file_id, filename, text index) can be re-anchored to clause level by string match.
falseAssumptions.correction: Send clause passages inline and require verbatim quotes in a strict JSON field, then exact-match each quote in code; show OpenAI-route claims UNVERIFIED until they resolve.

falseAssumptions.claim: Prompts under 512 tokens are not cached on 5.x models (all 5.x models have a 512 minimum).
falseAssumptions.correction: Keep the minimum cacheable length per model id in the versioned capability table; caches are isolated per workspace.
